questions.explanation: Moles = molarity x volume = 1 x 2 = 2 moles.

questions.question: A colloidal solution of liquid into liquid is known as:
questions.explanation: A liquid dispersed in a liquid is an emulsion.

questions.question: An example of completely immiscible liquid pair is:
questions.explanation: Water (polar) and benzene (non-polar) do not mix.

questions.question: A 15% W/W KOH solution can be prepared by mixing 15 g KOH in:
questions.explanation: 15 g KOH + 85 g water = 100 g solution, so it is 15% w/w.

questions.question: Number of moles of solute dissolved in 1 kilogram (1000 g) of solvent is:
questions.explanation: This is the definition of molality.

questions.question: Scattering of light beam path by colloidal particles is called:
questions.explanation: This is the Tyndall effect.

questions.question: Continuous zigzag motion of colloidal particles in suspension is:
questions.explanation: This random zigzag motion is Brownian movement.

questions.question: Concentration unit independent of temperature changes is:
questions.explanation: Molality uses mass of solvent, which does not change with temperature.

questions.question: Colligative properties of a solution depend strictly upon:
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles.

questions.question: Least entropy (minimum disorder) is found in which state of water:
questions.explanation: Ice has the most ordered arrangement and hence the least entropy.

questions.question: Energy change in Li<sup>+</sup><sub>(g)</sub> + Cl<sup>-</sup><sub>(g)</sub> → LiCl<sub>(s)</sub> is labeled as:
questions.explanation: Formation of an ionic solid from gaseous ions releases lattice energy.

questions.question: Which of the following change is NOT an endothermic reaction:
questions.explanation: Combustion releases heat, so it is exothermic.

questions.question: Heat transfer cannot occur across boundary of:
questions.explanation: An isolated system exchanges neither matter nor energy.

questions.question: Which enthalpy change (ΔH) is ALWAYS negative:
questions.explanation: Combustion is always exothermic, so ΔH is always negative.

questions.question: Standard enthalpy of formation of element at 25°C, 1 atm is zero EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Elements in their standard (most stable) form have ΔH<sub>f</sub> = 0. Diamond is not the standard form of carbon; graphite is.

questions.question: In First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔE = q + w), state function depending on initial/final state is:
questions.explanation: Internal energy is a state function; q and w are path functions.

questions.question: Which statement is incorrect:
questions.option_a: For constant pressure, ΔH = ΔE + PΔV
questions.explanation: For exothermic reactions, ΔH is negative (ΔH < 0).

questions.question: In thermochemical process, work done (w = -PΔV) is zero if system kept at:
questions.explanation: At constant volume ΔV = 0, so w = 0.

questions.question: Volume is a:
questions.explanation: Volume depends only on the state of the system and is an extensive state function.

questions.question: Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation is an application of:
questions.explanation: Hess's law follows from the first law (conservation of energy).

questions.question: Enthalpy change when 1 mole of substance completely burns in excess oxygen is:
questions.explanation: This is the definition of enthalpy of combustion.

questions.question: Unit conversion: 1 calorie is equal to:
A system exchanging heat with surroundings but NOT matter is a:
questions.explanation: A closed system exchanges energy but not matter.

questions.question: Degree of disorder or randomness in a chemical system is called:
questions.explanation: Entropy is the measure of disorder or randomness.

questions.question: Outer body of dry cell serves as anode and is made up of:
questions.explanation: The zinc container of a dry cell acts as the anode.

questions.question: Electrical conduction through electrolytic solution is due to flow of:
questions.explanation: Electrolytic conduction occurs through the movement of free ions.

questions.question: During electrolysis, reaction taking place at anode is ALWAYS:
questions.explanation: Oxidation always occurs at the anode.

questions.question: This statement is not correct for lead storage battery:
questions.option_d: Cathode is made of lead oxide
questions.explanation: The lead storage battery is a secondary (rechargeable) battery, not a primary one.

questions.question: In Zn-SHE cell, half reaction occurring at anode is:
questions.explanation: Zinc has a negative reduction potential, so it is oxidized at the anode.

questions.question: Strongest oxidizing agent in Electrochemical Series (E° = +2.87 V):
questions.explanation: F<sub>2</sub> has the highest reduction potential (+2.87 V).

questions.question: Galvanized iron rod is coated with a thin layer of:
questions.explanation: Galvanizing means coating iron with zinc.

questions.question: Fuel cell is a Galvanic cell based on reaction between:
questions.explanation: The common fuel cell uses the reaction of hydrogen with oxygen to form water.

questions.question: Oxidation number of Chromium in Na<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> is:
Which half cell reaction represents oxidation:
questions.explanation: Oxidation is loss of electrons, as in Zn → Zn<sup>+2</sup> + 2e<sup>-</sup>.

questions.question: Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) has standard potential assigned as:
questions.explanation: By convention, the SHE potential is exactly 0.0 V.

questions.question: Strongest reducing agent in Electrochemical Series (E° = -3.05 V):
questions.explanation: Lithium has the most negative reduction potential, so it is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.question: Salt bridge in a Galvanic cell maintains electrical neutrality by movement of:
questions.explanation: Ions flow through the salt bridge to balance charge in both half cells.

questions.question: Process of coating tin over iron sheets to prevent rusting is:
questions.explanation: Coating iron with tin is called electro-tinning.

questions.question: Chemical formula of Rust is:
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated ferric oxide, Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>·xH<sub>2</sub>O.
